problem: Prior foundation-model navigation methods use VLMs/LLMs zero-shot for planning or map annotation, converting visual input into abstractions (text, value maps). Web-trained VLMs lack spatio-temporal reasoning and embodied grounding, which limits path efficiency.
motivation: Semantic and open-vocabulary navigation needs both world knowledge and efficient, embodied decision making. Directly fine-tuning a VLM on raw egocentric history with simulated embodied data could ground the pre-trained knowledge without information bottlenecks, while still generalizing to unseen categories.
key_idea: Fine-tune a Mamba-based VLM (Cobra 2.8B) as a frontier-selection policy that takes raw egocentric video history, the language or image goal, and frontier images as input, and trains on a diverse mix of ObjectNav, OVON and ImageNav data plus an auxiliary spatial reasoning task.
insight: Diverse training data matters: the ablation shows ObjectNav-only already gives strong OVON zero-shot transfer (39.4 SR / 22.5 SPL on val unseen) thanks to VLM pre-training. Adding ImageNav (many more scenes, many goal embeddings) and OVON improves the OVON splits. The auxiliary spatial task gives the largest extra gain (HM3D-v0.2 74.9/39.2 -> 77.0/41.3 SR/SPL), suggesting that spatial correspondence learning helps frontier choice.
method: Frontier-based policy: build a 2D occupancy map from depth and odometry, extract frontiers, and let the VLM output the letter token of the chosen frontier; a pre-trained DD-PPO PointNav policy executes the waypoint.

Frontier representation: each frontier is a past RGB frame from the current episode, chosen at the pose whose view direction is most perpendicular to the frontier boundary, so there is no train/inference gap.

VLM architecture: Cobra (Mamba, 2.8B) with a frozen SigLIP ViT and trainable linear projector. History of up to 20 frames is average-pooled over H, W and time; static images are pooled over H and W only. Mamba gives faster inference (0.2s vs 0.32s) and lower memory.

Data generation: a greedy frontier-exploration oracle goes to the nearest frontier and switches to the goal-leading frontier when the goal is near. It is run on ObjectNav/OVON (145 scenes) and ImageNav (800 scenes); sizes are about 26k, 26k and 40k samples.
Auxiliary spatial task: given the video history and candidate images, answer 'Which part of the environment is located at (X,Y)?' (about 30k samples).
Training: next-token cross-entropy, AdamW at 2e-5, batch size 576, 3 epochs on 8 A40 GPUs (~15h); the LLM and projector are trained while SigLIP stays frozen.
Detection and stopping: OWLv2 detects the goal, MobileSAM segments it, and the PointNav policy approaches and stops within the success distance.

setting.backbone: Cobra 2.8B Mamba VLM (fine-tuned) with frozen SigLIP ViT; pre-trained DD-PPO PointNav low-level policy; OWLv2 + MobileSAM detection
setting.training_data: Habitat-generated oracle data: ~26k ObjectNav, ~26k OVON, ~40k ImageNav, ~30k auxiliary spatial samples, from HM3D train scenes
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D + odometry (pose relative to start); RGB history of up to 20 frames
setting.action_space: VLM picks a frontier (high-level), converted to a 2D waypoint; low-level discrete actions forward 0.25 m, turn 30°, stop
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT used only for oracle training data generation)

results: FiLM-Nav reaches 37.3 SPL and 61.7 SR on HM3D-v0.1, beating the best open-vocabulary baseline WMNav (31.2 SPL) and even PIRLNav in SPL (34.1). On HM3D-v0.2 it gets 77.0 SR / 41.3 SPL versus Uni-NaVid's 73.7 / 37.1. On OVON it has the best SPL on all three splits (24.5 / 23.1 / 24.4) and the best SR on two of three; Uni-NaVid has the higher Synonyms SR (43.9).
limitations: The 2D frontier mapping cannot handle stairs, so ~13.9% of HM3D-v0.1 episodes that require floor transitions fail.
It depends on an external object detector for termination and an explicit occupancy map. It only finds any instance of a category and handles single-object goals.
There is no real-robot deployment; real-world evidence is only offline frontier selection on recorded video and RealEstate10K.
